A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BRIDGE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Existing content can be matched across layout changes and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, IRT calibration, human-time prediction comparisons, and capability forecasts, including additional results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a response-sparsity experiment in Section 4.5 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The Bayesian 2PL IRT fitting procedure, METR-based log-linear time calibration, and frontier-horizon estimation remain unchanged. The new sparsity experiment tests the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use METR, SWE-bench Verified, MLE-bench, GDPval, and Cybench with the same task coverage. The sparsity experiment subsamples existing responses without introducing another dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Figures 3 and 4 retain the same comparators: Logit Success Rate, Gemini 3 Pro, and GPT-5.2. The model evaluation coverage in Appendix A is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 introduces a protocol that randomly removes 10–70% of observed responses, refits IRT, and measures Spearman correlations against full-data parameter estimates. Existing benchmark evaluation settings and forecasting procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis of whether incomplete response coverage destabilizes task-difficulty and model-ability rankings. This supplements the retained analyses, including the 80% success-threshold investigation in Appendix B.2.

E5.justification: Figures 5 and 8 retain shaded bands but remove their identification as transformed standard errors. Figures 6 and 9 retain bootstrap 95% confidence intervals but omit the previously stated 2,000 resamples, frontier-model sampling unit, trend refitting, and percentile construction.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports sparsity results, including difficulty/ability correlations of 0.9735/0.9903 after 50% removal and 0.9424/0.9798 after 70% removal. Existing results remain unchanged, including calibration R² = 0.81, SWE-bench accuracy of 41.6%, and Cybench tolerance coverage of 12/13 tasks.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(3), and horizon calculations are unchanged. Section 3 expands the temporal-scaling motivation for the existing log-linear calibration, without adding a formal result or changing the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: grounding model-derived difficulty in human time, transferring that calibration across benchmarks, and recovering approximately six-month doubling of the 50% task horizon.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly interprets high correlations under random response removal as evidence that the original 51% coverage supports reliable estimation. Existing interpretations and limitations, including the GDPval judge caveat and human-time variability discussion, remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the deletion levels and refitting procedure for the new sensitivity experiment, while removing the detailed bootstrap recipe from Figures 6 and 9. Appendix evaluation instructions, prompt templates, token budgets, and the repository link destination are retained.

R1.justification: Several model/system-card references and the ReAct citation are removed. Positioning relative to prior IRT work, TaskSense, and Epoch AI remains unchanged; publication and bibliographic updates otherwise refer to the same works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and affiliation-formatting edits, expands the scaling explanation in Section 3, and inserts Section 4.5. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the robustness table, renumbers the model-coverage table, enlarges Figure 2, corrects the BRIDGE label in Figure 3, and rearranges Figure 7 into one row. Figures 6 and 9 move, and several captions are shortened; existing plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 4.5 provides useful empirical support for the previously asserted stability of IRT estimation with incomplete response coverage. This modestly strengthens the paper, although the experiment establishes ranking stability under random thinning rather than directly validating time-prediction accuracy. The benefit is partly offset by reduced uncertainty and bootstrap documentation in Figures 5, 6, 8, and 9.
